newsitem.title: USA: SNET sees $15-20 mln Year 2000 costs in '97.
newsitem.headline: SNET sees $15-20 mln Year 2000 costs in '97.

text.p: Southern New England Telecommunications Corp said Wednesday that it will spend $15 to $20 million this year to solve its year 2000 computer problem.

Chief Financial Officer Don Shaffian said the expenditures would be dilutive to SNET's earnings but that they were necessary to avert a problem that could spell disaster for the company's operations over the long-run.
Separately, Chairman and Chief Executive Dan Miglio said the current Wall Street analyst consensus earnings estimate of $3.00 per share for the 1997 year "looks reasonable to us."
Shaffian told reporters additional expenses would be necessary in 1998 and 1999 but he did not elaborate.
Both executives were speaking at a press briefing prior to the company's annual meeting here.

The additional spending will be used to reprogram computers to process dates correctly after December 31, 1999, a task that will involve cross-checking millions of lines of the company's previously written computer code.
